main_text.head: Ad Ornatissimum Dn. Respondentem.
main_text.p: FABRITI nostræ quondam pars maxima mentis, Nec nunc diviso corpore, crede, minor! Ut veniens à Te me nuper epistola grata, Et multum votis ante petita meis. Illa ut me docuit specimen Te grande laboris, Auctusq; in studiis edere velle Tui. Extemplo, solitæ gnarus virtutis & artis, Exilii, in tales os solüiq; sonos.
FABRITIUS nostrum dum sedulus intellectum Instituit celsâ disserere è cathedrâ, Non tam quantum nos, sed quantū intellegat ipse, Notum facundo cuilibet ore facit.

p.i: Studiorum suorum successum gratulatur, simulq; veteris amicitiæ testatur fidem,

page.notes: Large initial F in "FABRITI" and "FABRITIUS" is a decorated capital, joined to the following word. The "Auctusq;" and "solüiq;" forms are as printed. Long s rendered as plain s throughout. The verse lines are kept on separate lines within each stanza paragraph.
